newsitem.title: INDIA: Indo Gulf Fertilisers output to rise sharply.
newsitem.headline: Indo Gulf Fertilisers output to rise sharply.

text.p: Indian urea manufacturer Indo Gulf Fertilisers and Chemicals Ltd expects to raise output substantially in 1997/98 (April- March) after a shutdown marred 1996/97, its chief executive said on Tuesday.
It has set a urea production target of 930,000 tonnes in 1997/98 -- a capacity utilisation of 121 percent, managing director B.N. Puranmalka told reporters.
Urea production in 1996/97 fell to 668,000 tonnes from 896,000 tonnes a year earlier because of a three-month closure due to technical problems.
"The shutdown helped us to improve operating efficiency," he said after releasing the results for 1996/97. "Productivity will go up 8-9 percent 1997/98."

During 1996/97 urea sales totalled 3.72 billion rupees ($104 million) against 4.56 billion a year ago while trading in fertilisers and pesticides brought in 662.9 million against 1.10 billion in 1995/96, results released on Tuesday showed.
Puranmalka said urea sales in 1997/98 would rise to 5.18 billion rupees and trading activity another 1.28 billion.
It expects to achieve an operating margin, before provision for interest charges, depreciation and taxes, of 38 percent on urea sales and five percent in trading activity, he said.
Net profit in 1996/97 fell to 1.08 billion rupees from 1.45 billion in the previous year.
"The profits are below my expectations," said analyst Vivek Jain at ICICI Securities and Finance Company Ltd. "I had expected a net profit of 1.25-1.30 billion rupees."
The firm, a member of India's Aditya Birla group, hopes to commission a 100,000 tonnes per annum copper smelter in December which would boost total sales by 2.64 billion rupees in 1997/98.
"This will not add to profits though," Puranmalka said. "We hope to break even. It will result in higher depreciation write-offs and lower taxes."
The 18.50 billion rupee smelter plant is scheduled to achieve 70 percent capacity utilisation in 1998/99 contributing 9.9 billion rupees to the total sales.
Capacity utilisation will improve to 85 percent in 1999/2000 with additional sales at 12.8 billion rupees, he said.
At 100 percent capacity utilisation in the following year it will contribute 16 billion rupees to total sales, he said.

The copper plant would produce 100,000 tonnes of sulphuric acid as a by-product which the firm plans to convert into 200,000 tonnes of phosphoric acid, a raw material for fertiliser product diammonium phosphate, he said.
The company plans to raise 3.15 billion rupees through an equity issue in 1998/99.
"We are not planning an equity issue in the year 1996/97," Puranmalka said. "We would like to come at a time when we are in a position to give some comfort to the investor."
Asked whether it plans to raise equity overseas through issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs), he said: "We are open to both (domestic and foreign investors)."
The Aditya Birla group firm had raised $100 million through GDRs in January 1994. ($1=35.76 rupees)
